channel.title: AI Waterside Podcast
channel.description: A daily brief on AI models, tooling and the creator side of the industry — what shipped, why it matters, and what to do about it.
channel.itunes:author: Austin Peechatt

item.title: Thursday, October 15
item.description: • LFM2.5‑24B‑A2B — a 24‑billion‑parameter reasoning model that activates only two billion parameters per token, enabling fast, private on‑device assistants with 131 K token context and explicit chain‑of‑thought. • Claude Code — Anthropic's development extension for VS Code that adds inline virtual‑text hints, OpenTelemetry cache metrics, RTL support, and an /advisor command for quick assistance. • Folkbench Switch — a Tauri‑Rust desktop client that lets users toggle between AI proxy endpoints with one click, displaying live rankings for stability, latency, price and security. • New‑term‑radar — a daily scraper that monitors social feeds for emerging AI model, product or repository names, delivering early‑signal tables for content creators to gain first‑mover advantage. • Amp — a platform that wraps OpenAI’s latest agents, like GPT‑6 Astra and GPT‑Live‑1, into ready pipelines for scheduling, inventory and customer‑service automation. • Tree Appreciator — a tiny three‑js web game generated by Claude that lets players compare algorithmically grown trees, showcasing LLM‑driven rapid prototyping of interactive visual content.

item.title: Wednesday, October 14

item.title: Tuesday, October 13
item.description: • Meta's Muse Wonder — Meta's second‑generation frontier language model, offering fast and full‑scale tiers with 1 M token context for high‑throughput personal‑agent applications. • Folkbench — An open‑source Tauri‑based desktop client that lets users switch between AI API endpoints instantly, displaying latency, token usage and cost to optimise performance. • Codex CLI — A command‑line tool now bundled with a background daemon that auto‑updates, which can continue running after the terminal closes, potentially creating unwanted processes. • Web‑edit — A lightweight Python web app using CodeMirror that serves a folder over Tailscale, enabling secure mobile editing of files without exposing data to external services. • New‑Term‑Radar — A daily scraper that monitors early mentions of AI‑related terms across social platforms and surfaces emerging names before traditional keyword tools detect them. • Local AI — Running large language models on personal hardware, now feasible with Apple’s Mac Studio, RTX Spark GPUs and open‑source models like Hermes for private, on‑device assistants.

item.title: Monday, October 12
item.description: • Strands Decider — a system‑one decision model that ranks options and scores them on Apple‑silicon Macs, enabling low‑latency branching in agentic workflows. • Claude Code — Anthropic’s coding assistant for desktop and CLI, now with unified policy keys and auto‑compacting context to reduce token waste in long sessions. • Whirl — an open‑source full‑stack AI chat platform built with Next.js and Convex that provides modular memory, tool plugins and easy self‑hosting for custom assistants. • Autonomous FPS Decompiler — using Claude Max and Codex Pro to decompile a shooter into C++, proving multi‑model orchestration can deliver production code. • Hermes Agent — an open‑source local LLM stack that lets developers run multi‑billion‑parameter models on Mac hardware, offering privacy‑first inference and reducing reliance on cloud APIs. • X API Exhibit — a showcase of apps and Grok Bot templates that use X data, helping developers discover integration patterns and lower entry barriers.

item.title: Sunday, October 11
item.description: • Claude Code — Anthropic's coding assistant update adds a code policy key, auto‑compact windows and a unified workflow subagent model, cutting latency and context overload. • Strands Decider — a decision‑model library that picks and scores options in one inference pass, delivering faster results without training data, running efficiently on Apple‑silicon Macs. • Whirl — an open‑source AI chat app on Next.js and Convex that enables self‑hosted, memory‑aware conversations with search, analytics and tool integrations via API keys. • celld — Cloudflare’s first‑class Durable Objects implementation for the Deno runtime, providing object‑storage‑only coordination that lets developers self‑host Workers‑style services with built‑in durability. • Caddy and Comma — AI agents for iMessage and RCS that connect to calendars and email, allowing users to create events or manage to‑dos via text.

item.title: Thursday, October 8
item.description: • GPT‑6 — OpenAI's latest ChatGPT model with an Intelligent UI that adds interactive panels, buttons and live widgets inside the chat, enabling rapid prototyping. • Claude Haiku 5.5 — Anthropic's small, low‑cost model with an adjustable effort knob, offering fast, cheap performance for high‑volume tasks like log summarisation and short‑text classification. • Mistral Large 4 — Mistral AI's 7‑billion‑parameter model that balances speed and reasoning depth, suitable for single‑GPU inference and providing a modest upgrade over existing Mistral 7B deployments. • EmbeddingGemma 2 — A lightweight multimodal embedding model built on Gemma 4 that unifies text, code, image, video and audio vectors for on‑device, privacy‑first search. • AI System Design guide — An open‑source, step‑by‑step notebook that shows how to build LLM‑centric retrieval, generation and autonomous‑agent pipelines, providing ready‑made scaffolding and evaluation scripts. • Strands‑decider — A lightweight “system‑one” decision model supporting Apple‑silicon, CUDA and vision inputs, offering faster choice selection than full LLMs for routing and tool‑selection in agent workflows.

item.title: Tuesday, October 6
item.description: • Reflection Beam — an open‑source 501‑billion‑parameter text model for coding, agentic tasks and scientific work, offering near‑state‑of‑the‑art performance on commodity hardware. • Whirl — a self‑hostable full‑stack AI chat application built on Next.js and Convex that lets you plug any LLM, persistent memory and tools, enabling rapid internal chatbot prototypes. • AI System Design — a curated open‑source tutorial collection that walks developers through building LLM pipelines, retrieval‑augmented generation and autonomous agents, accelerating product prototyping. • Instinct — an AI agent you can add to chats on iOS, Android or web, coordinating plans and tasks without requiring participants to install app. • TikTok AI shopping assistant — a conversational tool that guides users through product details, sizing and checkout, keeping commerce inside the TikTok feed and streamlining purchases. • Cowork cloud version — moves model inference and the VM to remote servers, giving uninterrupted performance across devices and enhancing security by isolating sessions.

item.title: Sunday, October 4

item.title: Saturday, October 3
item.description: • Gemini 4 Argon — Google DeepMind's new large model with a million‑token window, enabling whole‑codebase reasoning and complex multi‑step tasks. • Claude Code — Anthropic's coding assistant update adds UI shortcuts, in‑session GitHub API calls, and prompt recovery to streamline debugging. • AI System Design — a community‑curated repository that provides runnable notebooks and Docker configs for building production‑grade LLM, RAG, and agent pipelines. • Strands Decider — a lightweight decision‑model library that strips the generation head from a decoder LLM, delivering millisecond‑scale scored choices for real‑time pipelines. • Meta’s Muse Gadgets — open‑source firmware and Linux SDK let developers attach Meta’s personal AI assistant to cheap hardware, creating custom voice‑controlled peripherals. • GPT‑6 model guide — a concise playbook that consolidates community best practices for selecting variants, tuning reasoning depth, and safely orchestrating tool calls.

item.description: • Meta’s Muse Gadgets — an open‑source kit that lets developers attach hardware to Meta’s personal AI agent, enabling tangible actions such as scheduling meetings or controlling lights. • Gemini 4 Argon — Google DeepMind’s frontier model with million‑token context, allowing extremely long, multi‑step reasoning for tasks like code reviews or legal research. • GPT‑6 model guide — a concise playbook that helps startups select the appropriate GPT‑6 variant, tune reasoning depth, and integrate tools into production pipelines. • Claude Code — an update that adds a fullscreen text‑selection helper, built‑in GitHub API, and prompt recovery shortcut, reducing friction for developers using Claude for coding assistance. • AI System Design — an open‑source collection of lessons and runnable code that guides building LLM‑powered retrieval, generation, and autonomous‑agent pipelines, accelerating prototype to production. • Strands Decider — a system‑one decision model from Strands that replaces the language head with fast option scoring, delivering sub‑second choices for agentic workflows.
item.content:encoded:
• Meta’s Muse Gadgets — an open‑source kit that lets developers attach hardware to Meta’s personal AI agent, enabling tangible actions such as scheduling meetings or controlling lights.
  • Gemini 4 Argon — Google DeepMind’s frontier model with million‑token context, allowing extremely long, multi‑step reasoning for tasks like code reviews or legal research.
  • GPT‑6 model guide — a concise playbook that helps startups select the appropriate GPT‑6 variant, tune reasoning depth, and integrate tools into production pipelines.
  • Claude Code — an update that adds a fullscreen text‑selection helper, built‑in GitHub API, and prompt recovery shortcut, reducing friction for developers using Claude for coding assistance.
  • AI System Design — an open‑source collection of lessons and runnable code that guides building LLM‑powered retrieval, generation, and autonomous‑agent pipelines, accelerating prototype to production.
  • Strands Decider — a system‑one decision model from Strands that replaces the language head with fast option scoring, delivering sub‑second choices for agentic workflows.
